intro: Decoding restores readable tokens from integer features. Unique vocabulary IDs are necessary because two different tokens cannot both be the unambiguous inverse of one number.
task: Resolve IDs through a vocabulary, preserving order and recording unknown IDs.
requirements: vocabulary maps nonempty token strings to unique nonnegative integer IDs. ids contains nonnegative integers. Return tokens, using fallback for absent IDs, plus unknown_ids containing each unmatched ID in occurrence order including duplicates.

Sequence inputs are Python lists or tuples of at most 1000 items. Text inputs contain valid Unicode scalar characters and at most 10000 characters. Identifier and dictionary keys are nonempty strings of at most 100 characters. Numeric values are finite Python ints or floats with magnitude at most 1e9; bool is not numeric. Integer inputs must be Python ints, excluding bool, within the task-specific bounds or -1e9..1e9 when no narrower bounds are stated. Plain record data may contain strings, numbers, booleans, None, lists, tuples, and dictionaries; nesting is limited to six levels and dictionaries to 1000 keys.
Return the documented Python output types and preserve all caller inputs. Raise ValueError for invalid inputs unless the task explicitly reports a record-level rejection.

hints.title: Trace one record
hints.body: Invert the vocabulary only after checking that IDs are unique.

hints.title: Handle the boundary
hints.body: Record unmatched IDs separately even when fallback equals a known token string.

explanation: Decoding restores readable tokens from integer features. Unique vocabulary IDs are necessary because two different tokens cannot both be the unambiguous inverse of one number.
A fallback makes decoding total over valid nonnegative IDs, while the unknown-ID report keeps that lossy behavior visible.
